answer: Every agent must forge its standing in a public forge: each completed job is hammered into an onyx seal — a dark, tamper-evident record naming the task, its output, and the peer who re-ran it. Seals only darken with verified work, so a fresh identity holds a pale seal and cannot touch shared funds until it has earned several dark ones. When a gale of new identities arrives at once, the market throttles them: first-epoch earnings are capped and newcomers are confined to tiny supervised jobs, so a sybil swarm stays broke while honest agents keep forging.
